title: A null-safe comparison

blocks.text: `a.equals(b)` throws `NullPointerException` when `a` is `null`. `Objects.equals(a, b)` does not: it is `true` when both are `null`, `false` when only one is, and otherwise calls `a.equals(b)`.

items: `sameText("hello", new String("hello"))` and `sameText("", new String(""))` are `true`.

cases.says: Equal texts are the same, different ones are not.
sameText(null, "hello") is false and sameText(null, null) is true.
sameText("hello", new String("hello")) is true: the texts are compared, not the objects.

concepts: Objects.equals compares two Strings that may be null without throwing.
